summary: Backend-only regression verification after full Telegram removal from /app/backend/routes/chat.py (send_telegram_notification, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/TELEGRAM_API constants, both call sites in /send and /send-image, httpx import) and removal of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from backend/.env plus dropping the telegram_subscribers collection. Ran the existing chat suite (21/21), a NEW dedicated telegram-removal regression suite (26/26 incl. real multipart image upload, image serving, path traversal, unread/read-marking), and the full security suite (414/414). Total 461/461 passed. Backend imports and starts cleanly with no ImportError/NameError; zero outbound Telegram HTTP calls in logs during the run (all api.telegram.org log lines are historical from April 2026). Telegram is confirmed fully gone: 0 references in any application .py file, 0 TELEGRAM keys in backend/.env, telegram_subscribers collection absent, and /api/chat/telegram/webhook returns 404 for POST/GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.

minor.issue: Unauthenticated request with a missing/malformed JSON body returns 422 (Pydantic body validation) instead of 401, because the SendMessage body model is resolved before the manual Authorization header check. Pre-existing FastAPI dependency-ordering nuance, not caused by the Telegram edit. With a valid body and no token it correctly returns 401. Low impact (schema shape disclosure only); consider moving auth into a dependency so 401 always precedes 422.

The now-removed Telegram bot token is still present in plaintext in historical log lines in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log (e.g. 'POST https://api.telegram.org/bot8658978837:AAETK-...'). Removing it from .env does not invalidate it. Recommend revoking/regenerating the bot via BotFather (or deleting the bot) and rotating anything else that appeared in logs.

action_items: No functional fixes required for the Telegram removal - it is complete and regression-free (461/461 backend tests passing).

SECURITY (outside this change, recommended): revoke/delete the old Telegram bot token 8658978837:AAETK-... via BotFather; it is still valid and is exposed in historical backend log lines even though it was removed from .env.

OPTIONAL hardening: refactor the repeated Authorization-header parsing in routes/chat.py into a shared FastAPI dependency so 401 is returned before 422 body validation and to remove the 6x duplicated auth block (DRY).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/chat.py is clean of Telegram: no TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/TELEGRAM_API constants, no send_telegram_notification definition or call sites, and the unused httpx import is gone. Remaining imports (os, uuid, logging, FileResponse) are all used.

DRY violation: the identical 6-line 'if not authorization or not authorization.startswith("Bearer ") ... decode_token ... 401' block is duplicated in all 5 protected chat endpoints. Extract into a reusable Depends() dependency.
The `logger` created at module top of chat.py is now unused after the Telegram notification code (its only consumer) was deleted - harmless dead code, safe to drop.

/send-image validates only the file extension, never the magic bytes or a max size. An attacker can upload arbitrary content (e.g. HTML/SVG payload or a multi-GB file) renamed to .png. FileResponse guesses Content-Type from extension so stored-XSS risk is low, but an explicit size cap is advisable.
Path traversal defense on /image/{filename} is correct (os.basename + realpath prefix check) and verified against encoded ..%2f, %2e%2e%2f and ....// payloads.
All chat responses correctly project out MongoDB _id ({'_id': 0}); asserted explicitly in the new tests.
